LanguageData.RR_Route_BuildBatteryDesc: Construct a battery on the gate's own circuit and charge it. The ordinary way, and the cheapest if the branch has steel and somebody to do the work.
LanguageData.RR_Route_BindExistingLabel: Bind a battery you already have
LanguageData.RR_Route_BindExistingDesc: Designate an existing battery as the gate's reserve. Nothing new is built; a battery that was already powering something else is re-purposed, which costs the branch whatever it was doing before.
LanguageData.RR_Route_AssembleOnSiteDesc: Run the assembly bill on the branch's own machining table and calibrate the result. Slower, and it leaves somebody on the branch who understands how the gate is put together.
LanguageData.RR_Route_RequisitionAssemblyDesc: Order the parts through the corporate catalogue and skip the fabrication. Faster and more expensive, and nobody on the branch learns anything from it.
LanguageData.RR_Route_SurveyAndAnalyseLabel: Survey a coordinate and analyse the book
LanguageData.RR_Route_SurveyAndAnalyseDesc: Send a crew through with a blank book, bring it home to a linked archive shelf, and put it through the laboratory. The intended route, and the one that earns insight as well as payment.
LanguageData.RR_Route_RecoverExistingRecordLabel: Recover a record already down there
LanguageData.RR_Route_RecoverExistingRecordDesc: Somebody else wrote one before you arrived. Find it, carry it out and file it. No survey of your own is needed, and you learn less about the coordinate it came from.
LanguageData.RR_Route_PlaceMarkersDesc: Set glow pods down at the junctions that matter and mark them as the route home. Three is what the company considers a minimum for a coordinate worth returning to.
LanguageData.RR_Route_CrewKnowsTheWayLabel: Your crew already knows the way
LanguageData.RR_Route_CrewKnowsTheWayDesc: A completed route log is proof that somebody walked it and wrote it down. The company will take that instead of markers, though the next crew will not thank you for it.
LanguageData.RR_Route_AnalyseDistortionDesc: Put a book through the laboratory that carries a record of the space misbehaving. The strongest evidence, and the only one that also advances the ladder.
LanguageData.RR_Route_TwoAccountsLabel: Two accounts of the same room
LanguageData.RR_Route_TwoAccountsDesc: Where a branch has a completed distortion log, the people who were there can speak to it directly. Cheaper than another expedition and worth less to the buyer.
LanguageData.RR_Route_CompleteFieldStabilityDesc: Finish the second rung of the ladder. The window gets longer because the branch understands why it was short, which is the outcome the company actually wants.
LanguageData.RR_Route_BuyTheWindowDesc: Order enough components through the catalogue to over-build the reserve and hold the window open by brute force. It works, it is expensive, and it teaches the branch nothing.
LanguageData.RR_Route_DeclareADirectionLabel: Tell them where this is going
LanguageData.RR_Route_DeclareADirectionDesc: Name the direction the branch intends to take and the company writes it down. Nothing is forfeited by choosing; the other directions stay open.
LanguageData.RR_Route_ShowThemByDoingDesc: Announce nothing. Go and meet something down there, write it down, and let the record speak for the branch. The company reads the file either way.
LanguageData.RR_Route_CommitToTheLadderDesc: Push the gate itself rather than the business around it. The branch that does this first is usually the branch that later regrets how wide the door was.
LanguageData.RR_Route_PurchaseDesc: Buy the shortfall through the corporate catalogue instead of recovering or building it. Available because the branch's catalogue carries this, and it costs money rather than work.
LanguageData.RR_Route_TestifyLabel: Have the crew account for it
LanguageData.RR_Route_TestifyDesc: Somebody on this branch has already been there and the log proves it. The company accepts a staff account in place of another expedition. Available because the branch has completed a log of the right kind.
LanguageData.RR_Event_FacilityRelief: A corporation clean-up team cleared the site, requisitioned a replacement crew and left supplies. The branch is open again.
LanguageData.RR_Relief_Body:
The parent corporation does not write off a branch it has on its books.
A clean-up team came in on all-access passes, removed {1} hostiles from the site and left. Behind them: {0} replacement staff and enough supplies to start again.
Nobody asked {2} whether it wanted the help, and no invoice came with it. The crew are on the ordinary wage from today.
LanguageData.RR_Event_CorporationContact: The parent corporation has this branch on the books. It is now an investment rather than an experiment.
